content.text:
The explorer's report landed and it settles several open questions — the syllabus lives in three places (the `UPCOMING` array, the masterclass specs, the digest DB model), the blog machinery is wired but orphaned, and `apps/docs` (Mintlify) is untouched boilerplate with zero project content. I have everything needed to shape the proposal. Here it is — this is a design round, so I'm presenting the shape and stopping for your yes before anything gets built.

---

## The recommendation in two sentences

Give the collection the shape of a **numbered, serialized web book whose chapters are running instruments**: one flat contents page at `/exhibits`, one route segment per exhibit at `/exhibits/<slug>`, all driven by a single syllabus registry — not a Mintlify-style doc site, and not the landing page growing forever. The deciding fact isn't taste: **at least eight of the seventeen upcoming topics are made of routes** — parallel & intercepted routes, error/not-found, dynamic params, redirects, view transitions, i18n, ISR, navigation itself — so they physically cannot live on any single page; each exhibit must own a route segment, and the only open question was ever the shell around those segments.

## What grounds this

I read the landing page, `voice.md`, `design.md`, and had the repo swept. Things that shaped the proposal: the syllabus already exists in code (`UPCOMING`, 17 topics, plus 5 shipped exhibits — 22 chapters total); the site's words are already book-and-museum words (`chapter="01"`, "exhibits", a nav literally labeled "contents"); the digest has a real data model in MongoDB with a `misconception` field and a `series/part` structure, authored in `apps/app`; a local-MDX blog route is fully wired but linked from nowhere; `apps/docs` is dead Mintlify boilerplate ("Starter Kit", plant-store API); and the masterclass lives separately under `/learn/…`. Also: the contents nav, the `UPCOMING` list, and the per-demo `chapter` props are three hand-maintained copies of the same knowledge.

## Why not the two obvious shells

**The doc site (Mintlify shape — sidebar tree, categories, search).** Docs organize *reference*: you arrive knowing what to look up, and the sidebar is a filing cabinet. This collection organizes *arguments* — every exhibit is a rebuttal to a belief, sequenced by a teacher — and `design.md` is explicit that the feel is "a developer environment, not a course platform." A persistent sidebar is course-platform chrome, and it frames each page as *a page about* streaming. The whole identity of this site is that the page *is* the streaming. Interactivity in doc sites means embedded widgets simulating the feature; here the claim "nothing on this page is a mockup" has to hold on every surface. (Also: there's no sunk investment pulling this way — `apps/docs` is empty boilerplate.)

**The single growing page (the current trajectory).** Dies twice: at 22 exhibits the page's weight and the contents bar both collapse, and the route-shaped exhibits can't board at all. The nearest variant — keep landing sections but hang auxiliary demo routes off them — splits each exhibit's home from its body and ruins per-exhibit shareability.

**The book (recommended).** The spine register of the site is already Matthew Butterick, and *Practical Typography* is the existing artifact closest to what this should feel like: a self-published web book, spare chrome, a table of contents and chapters, the artifact itself demonstrating its subject. This is that, except the chapters run. The Monday cadence makes it a *serialized* book — chapters ship weekly, the bound volume accretes, numbers are accession order. (If the wall ever gets crowded, thematic shelving can come later — the number stays, the shelf can move. Not now; 22 rows fit on one screen.)

## The design

**One registry.** A `syllabus.ts` in the web app — number, slug, topic, belief, status, shipped date per exhibit — replacing the three hand-maintained lists. It drives the contents page, the landing roadmap, the contents nav, prev/next links, the sitemap, and each page's metadata. Shipping an exhibit becomes: merge the folder, flip the registry entry.

**The contents page, `/exhibits` — a floor plan with the lights on.** The syllabus made navigable: shipped chapters as rows (number, belief as the link text — an index of things you were sure about — topic eyebrow), upcoming ones as the `+` rows the roadmap already renders, the next Monday marked. The distinctive move no doc sidebar can make: where it's cheap and true, a row carries **one live value from the running exhibit** — the cache row wears the current bake fingerprint, the mutation row the press count — each row Suspense-streamed, so the index itself is an instrument panel and, incidentally, a PPR demonstration. Digest capture at the bottom; this page's visitors are the most convertible ones.

**The exhibit page — the chapter anatomy, scaled up from `DemoSection`.** Belief as the H1, the intro escort at full length, the instrument(s) in the fixed chassis, the aside, the reference bar — plus what only a dedicated page affords: child routes when the topic *is* routes (the address bar joins the instrument — the masterclass's `address-strip.tsx` already prototyped this), a **making-of strip** linking the PR and the checkpoint transcript (no docs site on earth has this), prev/next by number, and its own OG card drawn by the existing `/api/og` with the belief as the title — which quietly makes exhibit 05's central claim, "one file draws the card for every page you will ever publish," literally true across the whole collection. The exhibit page's prose is the write-up's permanent public home; the Monday email stays the letter version with the banked reveals (`design.md` §5 banks them for exactly this).

**The landing page's new job: front door, not the whole building.** Nothing moves. The five built exhibits stay inline — they're the best sales material the site has — but their demo wrappers get extracted from `page.tsx` so each also renders at its own `/exhibits/<slug>`, giving every chapter a canonical URL from day one (a senior can drop `/exhibits/caching` into a code review instead of explaining; that's the shareability requirement cashed out). The roadmap section becomes a live excerpt of the contents page. One copy line needs re-anchoring per `voice.md` §7: "A new demo lands on this page" is about to stop being true — it becomes a structural truth about the site, not the page.

**Monday, structurally.** Merge exhibit folder, flip registry entry, email links the exhibit URL, a stable `/latest` redirect always points at the newest chapter (and is itself redirect-exhibit material). First chapter on the new shape writes its own narrative beat: **exhibit 06, navigation & prefetching, whose specimen is the playground's own contents page** — the exhibit that explains why the site became multi-page, demonstrated by the pages it became.

**The doctrine that keeps it from becoming a doc site:** wherever possible, the collection's own chrome is built from the syllabus. The 404 page is the not-found exhibit. The vitals exhibit measures this site's real field data. The i18n exhibit is the `[locale]` segment everything already sits in. The flags exhibit flips something visible site-wide. View transitions arrive between exhibit pages the week that chapter ships. The playground grows by eating its own features — which is also the honest version of "interactive."

## What it deliberately isn't

No embedded sandbox or editable REPL — a sandbox runs a *copy*, and the site's entire authority is that you're poking the production feature itself; hands-on is the cohort's job and the public repo's. No search until the contents page outgrows a screen. No per-level modes. No new CMS — exhibits are code, and code-as-content is the product.

## Named trade-offs

More upfront structure than stacking the landing page (registry, contents page, five thin pages, one extraction refactor) — amortized by every Monday after. Per-page metadata/a11y/OG polish becomes a repeated cost — the registry and shared chassis absorb most of it. Live contents rows add server work to the index — bounded by using only values that are already cached or one cookie read, and rows degrade to plain.

**Housekeeping the sweep surfaced** (separate, whenever): `apps/docs` is deletable dead weight, `(counter)/` is orphaned, `/pricing` is off-voice next-forge boilerplate, and the wired-but-unlinked blog could later serve as the digest archive (the `series/part` model already anticipates one).

---

**Your call.** Does the book shape get a yes? Three decisions inside it I'd like your explicit word on: **(1)** the URL word — I recommend `/exhibits` over `/playground`, `/demos`, `/x`; **(2)** the five landing exhibits also getting their own canonical pages via extraction — recommended, since a collection whose first five chapters are anchor links undercuts the grammar; **(3)** live values on contents rows — recommended, it's the single most "this could only be hasToggle" element of the index. Nothing gets built until you say so.

content.text:
The naming screen is up in your tab (same URL). Three candidates, each shown as a real address, pasted into a PR comment, and as the contents-page title. My reasoning:

**The principle:** an address names a place, so it wants a noun — and voice.md already reserves "poking" as the verb for the hero, CTA, and footer. Verbs make CTAs; nouns make addresses.

**A — `/lab` (recommended).** It's not imported — it's the site's own shipped self-description: the FAQ's answer to "What exactly am I looking at?" ends "this is the lab bench that belongs next to them." It's a word engineers use without irony, it passes the four-audience test evenly (school labs for the aspiring, GitHub-Next-style labs for the senior), and it makes design.md's existing vocabulary literal instead of metaphorical — instruments and specimens live in a lab. `hastoggle.dev/lab/caching` pasted into a code review is exactly the right temperature.

**B — `/poke`** is the most distinctively hasToggle, but it spends the one brand verb on chrome, and an imperative address runs slightly hot in serious sharing contexts.

**C — `/proof`** is rooted in the deepest belief — every sentence checkable — and reads brilliantly in a PR ("proof: …"). Its risk is that it makes the promise before the panel loads, and voice.md §4's "claim more than the panel proves" sits close by.

**The also-rans, and why each fell:** `/press` ("what happens when you press things") collides with press-kit; `/bench` with benchmarks; `/run` with CI runs; `/live` is an adjective and currently occupied by the masterclass redirect; `/on` (hastoggle.dev/on/caching, essay-style) is precious; `/toggles` echoes the brand but the demos aren't toggles; `/beliefs` or `/misconceptions` would label the confrontation, which §4 forbids outright — the title is the confrontation, the URL mustn't announce it.

One scope note: this decides the **URL word only**. The prose word ("exhibit" appears throughout the shipped landing copy) can stay as-is for now — identifiers and prose already diverge in this codebase (folders named `shell`, `stream` under topics named otherwise). Whether prose migrates from museum vocabulary to lab vocabulary is a separate copy decision we can take later, with voice.md open.

# The lab — approved design (2026-08-20)

Status: **approved by Eric** (companion session, 2026-08-20 evening). Untracked
by convention; this file is the build contract for whichever workspace
implements it.

Approvals on record: book shape ✓ · canonical pages for the five built
exhibits ✓ · live values on contents rows ✓ · URL word `/lab` ✓ ("lab is
perfect"). Rejected shells: doc-site (sidebar/reference posture), single
growing page. Rejected URL words: /exhibits (museum vocabulary), /poke
(spends the brand verb on chrome), /proof (overclaims before the panel
loads), /press, /bench, /run, /live, /on, /toggles, /beliefs (labels the
confrontation — voice.md §4).

## Shape

A serialized web book whose chapters run. One flat contents page at
`/[locale]/lab`, one route segment per exhibit at `/[locale]/lab/<slug>`,
everything driven by a single syllabus registry. Forcing fact: at least 8 of
the 17 upcoming topics are made of routes (parallel/intercepted, error/
not-found, dynamic params, redirects, view transitions, i18n, ISR,
navigation) and cannot live on any single page. Feel: Practical Typography
whose chapters execute — spare chrome, numbered chapters, prev/next, no
sidebar. The word "lab" is rooted in shipped copy: "the lab bench that
belongs next to them" (FAQ). Naming principle: the address names a place
(noun); "poking" stays the verb on the pages.

## Registry — `syllabus.ts` (apps/web)

One entry per chapter; single source of truth replacing three hand lists
(UPCOMING, ContentsNav CHAPTERS, DemoSection chapter props).

- `n` ("01"…), `slug`, `topic` (eyebrow text), `navLabel` ("The cache"),
  `belief` (present once shipped), `status: shipped | next | planned`,
  `shippedOn`.
- Drives: /lab rows + upcoming `+` list, landing Roadmap excerpt,
  ContentsNav, prev/next, sitemap entries, per-page metadata + OG title,
  `/latest` target (highest shipped `n`).

Slugs for the five (defaults, changeable in review): `boundary`, `caching`,
`streaming`, `server-actions`, `og-images`. Chapter 06 (next): `navigation`
(navigation & prefetching). Slugs are short, topical, stable forever —
internal folder names (shell, stream, mutation…) stay as they are.

## Contents page — `/lab`

- Shipped rows: number · belief (the link text) · topic eyebrow · one live
  value. `next` row marked (lands Monday, amber dot). Remaining topics as
  the `+` rows the landing roadmap already renders. Digest capture at the
  bottom.
- Live values, bounded: a shipped exhibit MAY export a small server
  component (`IndexValue`) from its folder; the row renders it inside
  Suspense; absent → plain row. Truth rule: the value must be literally
  true — 04's cookie count is per-visitor, so it reads as *your* presses,
  never a global count. 01: node version · 02: bake fingerprint + swatch
  (cached, shares the landing tag) · 03: static delay label · 05: static
  `1200 × 630 · png`.
- The index streams its rows — it is itself a PPR demonstration.
- Banked for chapter 06: hover-prefetch readout in the contents rows (the
  navigation exhibit's instrument living in the site chrome).

## Chapter page — `/lab/<slug>`

DemoSection grammar scaled to a page: belief as H1, topic eyebrow
(`02 · caching & revalidation`), intro at full walkthrough length (landing
intro is the trailer), the instrument chassis unchanged, the aside, the
reference bar. Plus what only a page affords:

- **Child routes** when the topic is routes — the exhibit owns its segment
  (error.tsx, [param], @slots, interceptors live inside it); the browser
  address bar joins the instrument.
- **Making-of strip**: PR · checkpoint transcript · prompts (links per
  exhibit; checkpoints repo already public).
- **Prev/next** by number, using `navLabel`.
- **Metadata/OG**: title from the belief; OG card drawn by the existing
  `/api/og?title=` — exhibit 05's "one file draws the card for every page"
  becomes literally true.
- The chapter page is the write-up's permanent public home; the Monday
  email stays the letter edition (banked reveals in design.md §5 are its
  exclusives).

## Landing page changes

- Extract the five wrapper functions (BoundaryDemo, ShellDemo, StreamDemo,
  MutationDemo, ImageDemo) from `page.tsx` into their `(playground)`
  folders; landing renders them unchanged (pixel-identical), chapter pages
  import the same wrappers. Shared instrument state across pages (the bake
  tag, the press cookie) is intended — "one entry, shared by every visitor"
  stays true.
- Roadmap section becomes a registry-driven excerpt linking to /lab.
- ContentsNav derives from the registry; gains a trailing link into /lab.
- Copy re-anchor (voice.md §7): DigestCTA's "A new demo lands on this
  page." stops being true when 06 ships elsewhere — rewrite via voice
  passes, structural phrasing.
- `/latest`: standing redirect to the newest shipped chapter (later:
  redirects-exhibit material).

## Monday runbook

merge exhibit folder → flip registry entry (planned → shipped, belief in) →
contents row lights up / roadmap shrinks / sitemap + OG appear (all
derived) → digest email links `/lab/<slug>` → `/latest` follows.

## Non-goals

No sandbox/REPL (a sandbox runs a copy; the site's authority is the real
thing running). No search until the contents page outgrows a screen. No
per-level modes. No new CMS — exhibits are code.

## Deferred / adjacent (not in scope)

- Prose vocabulary: "exhibit" stays in shipped copy for now; museum→lab
  migration is a separate copy decision taken with voice.md open.
- Digest public archive (DB model already has series/part/misconception);
  the wired-but-orphaned /blog could host it later.
- Housekeeping: apps/docs is dead Mintlify boilerplate; `(counter)/` is
  orphaned; /pricing is off-voice next-forge boilerplate.

## Build order (slices, each independently verifiable)

1. `syllabus.ts` + tests; ContentsNav, Roadmap, chapter props derive from
   it — landing visually unchanged.
2. Extract the five demo wrappers — landing pixel-identical, tests pass.
3. `/lab` contents page (plain rows) + sitemap + metadata + digest capture;
   its headline copy goes through voice.md's three passes with Eric.
4. Five chapter pages (wrapper + prose + making-of + prev/next + OG).
5. Live index values (Suspense) + `/latest` redirect. Cache-touching
   values verified on a preview deploy (design.md §6: dev lies).
6. Landing copy re-anchors (voice passes).

Verification: every slice ends with Biome + typecheck + the web app's
tests green, and anything touching `use cache` proven on a preview deploy,
not `next dev`.
